query: wat did he discover about lite
answer: Newton's biggest discovery about light was that white light is really a mix of all the colours. In the 1660s he shone sunlight through a glass prism and saw it spread into a band of colours, usually listed as red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. He then showed that the prism doesn't add those colours; it separates colours that were already in the light, because each one bends (refracts) by a slightly different amount [1][2][3]. This work also explained how rainbows form. It led him to build a reflecting telescope, which uses a mirror instead of a lens so it doesn't blur the image with colour fringes. He also studied the coloured rings that appear in thin films of air or glass, now called "Newton's rings" [3][4]. He published all of this in his 1704 book *Opticks*. In it he also argued that light is a stream of tiny particles, which he called "corpuscles." That particle idea was later replaced by the wave theory of light, but the book shaped research on light for more than a century [1][4].

sources.title: Isaac Newton and the Physics of Color: How a Prism Changed Everything
